## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

## Acceptance Criteria

(Canonical criteria — promoted from the producer-approved re-scope of 2026-11-09; they supersede the original AC1–AC6 recorded below. Original AC6 includes the `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard, which C6 relocates and updates.)

- **P1. No test lost or doubled** — suite runs the same 475 tests with identical per-file `unit`/`integration`/`e2e` membership as the `dev` baseline (unit 257 / integration 215 / e2e 3), verified by a before/after selection diff.
- **P2. Standard layout** — every `*.test.ts` lives under a top-level `tests/` tree (`tests/<area>/`, `tests/deploy/`, `tests/support/`, `tests/scripts/`); `tsconfig.json` includes `tests/**/*.ts`.
- **P3. Isolation preserved** — no Phaser/DOM file flattened into the node `unit` project; an equivalent deterministic membership guard passes.
- **P4. Aliases** — `@/*` → `src/*` resolves in `tsc`, Vite and Vitest; the classifier follows it.
- **P5. Tooling + docs** — test-skill type profiles (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) still run; comments, AGENTS.md and dev notes updated (CHANGELOG excluded — ship skill).
- **P6. Full suite passes.**

## Superseded original acceptance criteria (replaced 2026-11-09 by the P1–P6 re-scope above)

Retained for traceability only; NOT the completion gate — P1–P6 above are.

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and
   still passes.
4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles
   (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, `.pi/test-config.json`) remain
   functional — update only if project names/commands change, and verify each type
   (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) runs.
5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any
   dev notes reflect the new layout. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill).
6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is
  deliberately the single source of truth for selection; keep an equivalent guard).
- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore
  port, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0) into `tests/deploy/` for full parity — sequence after or
  alongside that port.

- **P5. Tooling + docs** — test-skill type profiles (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) still run; comments, AGENTS.md and dev notes updated (CHANGELOG excluded — ship skill).

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

# Intake brief — evaluate-tune-progress watchdog test races on src/data tune journal

## Headline

Point the `evaluate-tune-progress` real-CLI test at a per-test temp data
root so its watchdog assertions never read the shared `src/data` directory,
removing the last concurrent-run race window.

## Problem statement

The `--watchdog` case in `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` asserts on
state in the **real** `src/data` directory (the journal scan and the CSV
digest), so a sibling vitest worker that momentarily holds a journal there —
or edits the tracked CSV — can fail it spuriously. The observed flake
(`expected ['enemy-configs.csv.tune-journal'] to deeply equal []`) was
already mitigated once by scoping the journal assertion to the run's own pid
(commit `88e6827a`, AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS), but the test still reads the shared
directory, so AC1 of it ("the test no longer reads shared mutable state in
`src/data`") is not yet satisfied in letter and two narrow race windows
remain: an unparseable foreign journal counts as owned, and a sibling suite
doing a real-edit `--tune` spawn could transiently change the CSV between the
test's two digest reads.

## Users

As a **developer running the unit suite in parallel**, I want the
`evaluate-tune-progress` watchdog test to observe only its own run, so a
concurrent worker's transient journal (or edit) can never fail my build.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The CLI's `--tune` data root is overridable per run (a seam in
   `resolveTuneCsvPath()` in `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — e.g. an
   `EVAL_TUNE_DATA_ROOT` env override, or a `--tune-root <dir>` flag), so a
   test can point `--tune` at a temp directory holding a copy of
   `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` without touching the repo file.
2. The `--watchdog` cases in `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` run the
   real CLI against that per-test temp root; the CSV digest check and
   `journalsOwnedBy(run.pid)` assertions scan the temp root only — no read or
   write of `REPO_ROOT/src/data` remains in those cases.
3. Two concurrent full-suite `npm test` runs leave `evaluate-tune-progress`
   green (the shared-`src/data` race is eliminated structurally, not
   probabilistically).
4. Every other `evaluate-tune-progress` assertion still holds: per-run
   progress lines, no `[tune]` leak into stdout, four artifacts written, and
   the off-by-default and bad-budget (exit 2) cases.
5. The seam cannot silently diverge from the sweep's config reads: a
   redirected data root combined with a **value-changing** `--set` emits a
   stderr warning that the edit targets the redirected root while the sweep
   reads the bundled config store, and the seam is documented in the CLI
   `--help`/docs as a test-isolation hook.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A developer running `npm test` in parallel no longer sees a spurious
`evaluate-tune-progress` watchdog failure caused by another suite's
transient `src/data/*.tune-journal`.

## Constraints

- **Behaviour parity (gym↔game):** this is a test-isolation change to the
  `--tune` verification harness, not gameplay; no production game behaviour
  changes.
- **No silent divergence:** the candidate sweep's config reads go through the
  bundled config store (`src/data/*.csv` via Vite `?raw`, e.g.
  `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`), so a data-root override that only redirects
  the edit/journal target must be a documented test-isolation seam with a
  warning on value-changing edits — not a path for real tuning runs to point
  at a different CSV.
- Existing tests only ever issue **byte-level no-op edits** (`boss.health=1`),
  so redirecting the edit target is behaviour-identical for the suite; the
  seam must keep that true.
- Keep the change minimal: only `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and
  the CLI seam; do **not** refactor `evaluate-failfast.test.ts` or
  `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` (producer decision, Q2) and do not
  entangle the product-level concurrency work in AH-0MW25VH540078FDK.
- Work must happen in the worktree created by `implement.py start` (never the
  main checkout) per project rules.

## Existing state

- `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`: `CSV` is hard-coded to
  `resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'src/data/enemy-configs.csv')`; `csvDigest()` reads the
  real file; `journalsOwnedBy(pid)` does `readdirSync(join(REPO_ROOT,
  'src/data'))` and counts any journal whose recorded pid matches the spawned
  CLI, plus any unparseable journal (`catch { return true }`).
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (line ~428) hard-codes
  `resolvePath(import.meta.dirname, '..')` + `src/data` + `tuneFile`; there is
  no override today. `executeTune()` (line ~657) resolves the CSV, journals it
  before editing, and the `main()` reconcile (line ~804) restores stale
  journals for the resolved path.
- The observed flake predates the pid-scope fix; commit `88e6827a`
  (AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS) already scoped the journal assertion to the run's own
  pid, which is why reruns were green and the remaining gap is the letter of
  AC1 plus the two tight residual windows.

## Desired change

1. Add the data-root override to `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (env var preferred:
   zero public CLI surface, trivially injected via `cliSpawnEnv()` in
   `scripts/cliChildEnv.ts`; a `--tune-root <dir>` flag is the acceptable
   alternative and then needs `--help` + `evaluate.d.mts` + `docs/` sync).
2. In `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`: create a per-test temp data
   root (`mkdtempSync`), copy the shipped `enemy-configs.csv` into it, spawn
   with the override, and point `csvDigest()` and `journalsOwnedBy()` at the
   temp root (parameterise the dir instead of `REPO_ROOT/src/data`).
3. Emit the stderr warning in `executeTune()` when an override is combined
   with an edit whose `changed` is true; document the seam.

## Key Files

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — add the data-root override to
  `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (and the stderr warning near `attempt` in
  `executeTune()`).
- `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` — per-test temp data root; digest
  and journal assertions scoped to it; update the file-header comment.
- `scripts/cliChildEnv.ts` — inject the override env var per spawn.
- `scripts/evaluate.d.mts` — type the new option if a `--tune-root` flag is
  chosen.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` (crash-safe journal §) / `docs/EVALUATION.md` — document
  the test-isolation seam.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` / `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — referenced only
  to confirm the sweep read path (no change).

## Related work

- **AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS** (completed, `88e6827a`) — the pid-scoped
  `journalsOwnedBy` fix this item builds on; partial overlap, antecedent.
- **AH-0MVSE1OPF008G1SB** (completed) — per-run progress + `--watchdog`
  (parent of this test file).
- **AH-0MVSE1A7O002PXAO** (completed) — crash-safe tune CSV journal.
- **AH-0MW25VH540078FDK** (open) — serialise concurrent `--tune` runs on the
  same balance CSV (shared journal path); product-level, related, out of
  scope here.
- **AH-0MW0Q1DCZ006AUGP** (completed) — weapon catalogue CSV codec (the
  item that discovered this flake, `discovered-from:`).
- **AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7** (completed, epic) — data-driven weapon tuning.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the override is used only by tests, and existing test runs
  keep every edit a byte-level no-op, so no real tuning run is affected.
- **Risk:** a future test/run combines the override with a value-changing
  edit and silently tunes nothing → mitigated by the AC5 stderr warning and
  docs.
- **Risk (scope creep):** threading the override into the config store's
  `?raw` loads would make real edits honour the temp root but is far larger
  and touches production load paths — explicitly out of scope; the warning +
  docs approach is proportionate for a test-isolation seam.
- **Risk:** the CLI parses options from argv only today; an env override
  must be documented in the source and the file-header comment so future
  readers understand why the test no longer reads the repo dir.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (2026-11-13, asked by Map): "Scope: the pid-scope fix already closed the
  recorded flake; how should this item proceed? A) per-test temp data root
  (CLI seam) — recommended; B) close as already addressed; C) minimal
  hardening." — Answer (producer): **A**. Source: interactive reply on
  work item AH-0MW22FTXP004Z4G5 (comment AH-C0MWF28EGI0074O58). Research:
  verified `resolveTuneCsvPath()` hard-codes the repo data root and the
  config store reads CSVs via `?raw` imports, so a seam is required for A.
- Q2 (2026-11-13, asked by Map): "If A, also refactor
  `evaluate-failfast.test.ts` to a temp root, or only
  `evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`?" — Answer (producer): **only
  `evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`** (as recommended). Source: interactive
  reply. Constraint recorded above; failfast's edit discipline already holds
  and widening scope risks entangling AH-0MW25VH540078FDK.

## Goal

Make the dev-only telemetry recorder cheap enough that it does not distort a measured run.

**User story:** As a developer profiling the game, I want the dev telemetry recorder to stay out of the frame budget, so a profile measures the game and not the recorder.

## Scope

- Avoid serialising/redacting a payload that will be discarded for exceeding the upload cap (check the size first, or stream/bound the recording).

- Production telemetry behaviour (the recorder is dev-only).

The stress gym's `getPerformanceCounts()` override carries a comment claiming the mineral count is always zero, but the hardware-GPU verification runs (AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P) recorded non-zero live minerals in every report.

**Discovered from:** AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P (hardware-GPU desktop verification runs).

## Evidence

`src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts:291`:

> `minerals` is 0 because this gym deliberately seeds none.

Measured `counts` from the four 60 s hardware-GPU reports (`counts` sampled every 250 ms, 237 samples each):

| Host | Run | minerals peak | minerals mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| desktop browser | 1 | 8 | 1.20 |
| desktop browser | 2 | 7 | 2.11 |
| Electron | 1 | 1 | 0.55 |
| Electron | 2 | 2 | 0.95 |

The gym config does set `minerals: false` (`src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts:207`), so the field starts empty — the non-zero values accumulate during the window (most plausibly salvage dropped by enemies destroyed on contact with the player ship), which the comment does not anticipate.

## Expected behaviour

Either the comment/doc statement is corrected to "the field starts empty (no seeding) and can accumulate a handful of drops", or the gym actively clears the mineral field so the measured load really is enemies + bullets only. The first is documentation-only; the second changes the measured scene, so it needs its own before/after run.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts` no longer claims the mineral count is always 0, or the gym's measured mineral count is 0 in a 3 s guard-check run — one of the two, with the choice recorded.
2. `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`'s statement about the stress gym and minerals is consistent with the behaviour actually implemented (and with the counts blocks already published for AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P).
3. If the gym is changed to clear the field, a `--seconds 60 --warmup 3` `GymPerformance` run is recorded showing the scene still holds 100 enemies and ~200 live bullets.

## Out of scope

- Re-measuring the hardware baselines — they are recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` and are not invalidated by a comment fix.
data.title: GymPerformance counts comment says minerals is always 0, but hardware runs measure 1-8 live minerals

## Problem statement

The ring-timing CLI's operator-facing text report mixes per-seed and multi-seed
figures. `formatRingTimingReport` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) renders:

- means over the seed set for `deployments`, `measured runs`, `total`, `banked salvage` and `ring secured`;
- but **seed 1's own value** for `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` (`report.runs[0]?.retryMinutes`, `runs[0]?.betweenSortieMinutes`, `runs[0]?.retakeMinutes` / `runs[0]?.expectedRetakes`).

With the default three-seed evidence set the two halves of one report therefore
describe different populations.

## Evidence

`npm run ring-timing` (2026-11-11, worktree of AH-0MW9VATHR0003WTJ, exit 0):

```text
Ring 2 · grind · seeds 1, 2, 3
  retries            55.0 min
  total              116.4 min (min 112.7, max 123.4)
```

The committed artefact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, revision
`e873e8c3`) records per-seed `retryMinutes` of **55 / 50 / 55** — a mean of
**53.3**, not 55.0. `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* consequently
quotes "55 of its 116.4 min (≈47 %)", pairing seed 1's retry total with the
mean total (the mean-based share is ≈45.8 %). `between sorties` and
`exposed re-capture` happen to be seed-invariant today, so only the retry line
is visibly wrong — but the rendering is one bug, not one line.

## Expected behaviour

Every metric line in the text report describes the same population (the seed
set), consistent with the JSON artefact: mean plus min–max for the per-run
totals, or an explicitly labelled seed-1 sample. The report-rendering test
(`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` § *report rendering*) should pin a
multi-seed case where the seeds differ, so the mixing cannot return.

## Acceptance criteria

- `formatRingTimingReport` renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from the multi-seed aggregate (mean, with min–max where the JSON summary carries it), or labels them as a single seed; no line silently reports seed 1 as the seed-set figure.
- A report-rendering test feeds a multi-seed report whose per-seed retry totals differ and asserts the rendered value is the mean, not seed 1's.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* quotes the retry minutes and share from the aggregate consistent with the rendered report and the committed artefact.
- Full project test suite passes.

## Notes

- Found by the verification slice `Record the ring 2 before/after split and verify the acceptance criteria (AH-0MW9VATHR0003WTJ)`; deliberately not fixed there (that item's scope forbids code changes).
- No behaviour or measured value changes: this is a reporting/consistency fix only.
data.title: Ring-timing text report prints seed 1's retry, between-sortie and re-capture minutes as if they were the multi-seed figures

**Discovered while addressing AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9** (Hex War deployment loadout missing from the HUD upgrade list), discovered-from:AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9.

`applySceneSetup` (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) grants a capture/scripted setup's `player.weapons`, `player.timedWeapons`, `player.weaponLevels` and `powerUps` through the `Player` seam only. Gyms that render the shared HUD (`GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymWeaponLeveling`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, ...) build their upgrade rows from `EffectsRegistry.activeWeapons()`, so a captured permanent weapon is counted by `resolvePlayerSlotState(player)` (`Loadout n/6`) but has no row in the upgrade list.

The hangar-war deployment path has the same defect and is fixed in AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 by granting through the shared `grantPermanentWeapon` seam (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`). This item is the scripted-setup counterpart: route the setup applier through the same shared grant seam so a capture's loadout renders and behaves exactly like live play.

Note the documented divergence: the setup applier may pre-grant more than six kinds (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`) — that is intentional for capture and must be preserved (see `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 / AH-0MVVJS34M00551ES).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gym (or scene) that applies a capture setup containing permanent weapons reports one slot-counted HUD upgrade row per granted weapon, matching a live-play run granted the same weapons through `grantPermanentWeapon`.
- The setup applier's documented ability to pre-grant more kinds than `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` is preserved (the capture divergence is unchanged).
- A regression test covers a setup-granted permanent weapon reaching both the `Player` and the `EffectsRegistry`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
data.title: Capture/scripted setup grants loadout to the player only, so HUD upgrade rows omit it

# Budget verdicts and linked rebalancing items (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A child 4)

Parent: Re-measure ring timing for one-level hex deployments
(AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A). Prerequisite: **Regenerate the ring-timing baseline
artifact**.

## Context

The authored windows are ring 1 **40–60 min** and ring 2 **90–120 min**
(`RING_TIMING_TARGETS`), judged on the **grind** line with a 10 % tolerance of
each window's width (±2 min / ±3 min). One-level deployments should shrink ring
totals markedly (the retired model spent most of a deployment climbing campaign
levels past the hex's own), so a ring missing its window is the **expected**
outcome, not a defect in the new model — and the parent item's AC3 forbids
silently re-wording a missed budget: each missed ring becomes its own linked
rebalancing item.

Ring windows are **not** re-authored in this item: the harness records what the
shipped game measures, and a window change is a separate design decision.

## Desired change

1. Judge each ring's grind total from the regenerated artifact against its
   authored window and tolerance; state `in-window`, `within-tolerance` or
   `missed` per ring with the measured figure and the delta to the window.
2. For **each** ring that no longer holds, create a separate rebalancing work
   item carrying: the measured figure (mean + min–max), the window, the delta,
   the loss/retry/re-capture split that produces it, the before/after change
   attributable to the one-level model, and the options available (re-author the
   window, tune the authored ring data, revisit the retry/re-capture
   allowances) — leave the ruling to the producer. Link it with
   `related-to:AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A` and record the created ids on parent and
   this item.
3. Pin the verdicts in tests: the real-arena budget assertions in
   `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` reflect the regenerated numbers, and the
   ring-1/ring-2 verdicts are asserted explicitly so a future silent drift
   fails.
4. Do **not** change `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, the tolerance, the authored ring
   data or the allowances here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each ring's grind budget verdict is recorded with its measured mean, min–max, window and delta, and the regenerated artifact is the stated source.
- Every ring whose budget no longer holds has its own linked rebalancing work item (measurement, delta, split and options recorded; `related-to:AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A`), and its id is recorded on the parent item; if both rings hold, that is recorded explicitly instead.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` asserts the regenerated verdicts for ring 1 and ring 2 (grind) against the committed artifact and passes.
- Tests cover the new model: a per-level deployment ends at its level's wave-5 sortie clear and an early death is a loss (landed by the sibling test item), the report is deterministic for the same seeds/options, and the ring-1/ring-2 budget verdicts match the regenerated numbers.
- `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, `RING_TIMING_TOLERANCE_PERCENT`, the authored ring data and every allowance are unchanged by this item (`git show --stat` evidence in the completion comment).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- The full project test suite passes with the change.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` — the regenerated evidence the verdicts are read from.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — `RING_TIMING_TARGETS` / `RING_TIMING_TOLERANCE_PERCENT` (read-only: judged, not re-authored).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — the real-arena budget assertions pinned to the regenerated verdicts.

## Coordination (2026-11-13): the per-level deployment ends on wave 5

"Ends at its level's wave-10 clear" in the acceptance criterion above is
superseded: the shipped sortie (AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS, on `dev`) is five waves
— first four regular waves plus the wave-5 mini-boss composition, truncated by
`truncateCampaignForDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`,
`DEPLOYMENT_WAVE_COUNT = 5`). The new-model test line therefore reads "a
per-level deployment ends at its level's wave-5 sortie clear"; everything
else (verdicts, windows, tolerance, allowances) is unchanged.

## Verdicts (2026-11-13, regenerated artifact)

Source: `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, regenerated from the shipped code
by AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02 (`npm run ring-timing -- --json --out
docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, two runs byte-identical, sha256
`d8fb5775…`). Judged on the **grind** line, seeds 1–3, against the authored
windows and the 10 % tolerance (±10 % of each window's width: ±2 min ring 1,
±3 min ring 2). Windows, tolerance, authored ring data and allowances are
**unchanged** by this item.

| Ring | Verdict | Measured mean | Measured min–max | Window | Tolerance | Delta to window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **missed** | 16.4256 min | 15.7239 – 16.9144 min | 40–60 min | ±2 min | −23.5744 min below the floor (−21.5744 below the 38 min tolerance floor) |
| 2 | **missed** | 48.0967 min | 42.4067 – 58.4144 min | 90–120 min | ±3 min | −41.9033 min below the floor (−38.9033 below the 87 min tolerance floor) |

Split that produces each total (mean per run; total = deployment + between-sortie
+ retry + re-capture):

| Ring | Deployment (measured) | Between-sortie (2 min × hexes) | Retry (measured replay) | Re-capture | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.2128 | 12.0 | 2.2128 | 0.0 | 16.4256 |
| 2 | 12.0483 | 24.0 | 12.0483 | 0.0 | 48.0967 |

Every sortie on both grind lines is a first-attempt loss (0.0 captured, 6.0 /
12.0 losses per run) yet the ring still ends secured (3/3 runs). The rush lines
stay `not-applicable` for the budget (10.1 min ring 1, 22.3 min ring 2).

## Linked rebalancing items (created by this item)

Both rings miss, so each has its own linked rebalancing work item carrying the
measurement, the delta, the split, the before/after attributable to the
one-level model and the options — the ruling is left to the producer:

- Ring 1 — **AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X**, Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured
  16.4 min vs the authored 40–60 min window.
- Ring 2 — **AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5**, Rebalance ring 2's grind budget: measured
  48.1 min vs the authored 90–120 min window.

Both carry `related-to:AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A`, `discovered-from:AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V`,
stage `idea` and `needsProducerReview`. No window, ring data or allowance was
changed here: the two ids are also recorded as a comment on the parent
(AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A), and the docs requote is the sibling item
AH-0MWCQ4IS6001X7W3 (blocked on this one).

## Verdict pins landed by this item

`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` now asserts, per ring, the committed
artifact's `missed` verdict, measured mean, min–max, authored window,
tolerance, delta to the window floor and the split that produces the total
(ring 1 `16.4256` / ring 2 `48.0967`), re-judges the measurement through
`evaluateRingTimingBudget` and cross-checks the real-arena suite against the
artifact — so a future silent drift (a re-measurement or a balance change)
fails loudly. Code comments in `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` (`## Budgets`,
`RING_TIMING_TARGETS`) and the README's ring paragraph quote the verdicts and
the two linked item ids.

## Impact

A producer can see, from one place, that both ring budgets now miss their authored windows and by how much, with a dedicated rebalancing decision queued for each ring instead of a quietly re-worded budget.
data.title: Budget verdicts and linked rebalancing items

# Hangar Map UX

## Problem statement

The shipped Hangar War hex map (`AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2`) draws **every** hex of the
payload's ring regardless of reachability, labels tiles only with their aggression
(`AGG n`), keeps held hexes out of keyboard focus, colour-codes ownership with a
red/green scheme that is not colourblind-safe, and navigates linearly — so a player
cannot see reachable territory at a glance, cannot read coordinates or ownership on
the tiles, cannot inspect a hex they own, and cannot steer focus spatially. This
item tightens the map into a progressive, colourblind-safe, spatially-navigable
surface.

## Users

- **The Hangar War player** planning the next deployment from the map.
  - *As a Hangar War player, I want the map to show only hexes I can actually
    reach, so planning targets real next steps instead of far-future rings.*
  - *As a player, I want each tile to show its coordinates and whether it is mine or
    an enemy's without relying on colour, so I can plan and replay with confidence.*
  - *As a player, I want arrows to move me spatially around the map — and to reach
    the hangar — so keyboard navigation matches how the map looks.*
  - *As a player, I want to select a hex I already own to read its full intel
    (defender, pending attack, grant), while never accidentally re-deploying at it.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Adjacency-only reveal (producer Q1 = a).** A hex renders on the map only when
  it shares an edge with the hangar at `(0,0)` or with a hex the player holds; the
  hangar anchors the reveal, so ring 1 always renders and later rings appear
  progressively as their near neighbours are held. Hexes outside the reveal are not
  drawn and are unreachable by focus, click or the attract bot (the bot never falls
  back to a hidden hex).
- **Owned hexes selectable, never deployable.** A held hex can be focused/selected
  so the detail panel shows its full intel (defender, boss defeated, granted weapon,
  pending attack); activating a held hex performs **no** deployment. Unheld
  displayed hexes still deploy on activation (Enter/Space/click), unchanged.
- **CVD-safe ownership colouring (producer Q2 = b).** Tile text uses the CVD-safe
  pair — orange for enemy (unheld), blue for owned (held) — **plus** a non-colour
  per-tile discriminator (e.g. a filled/hollow marker glyph) so ownership is
  readable without colour. Owned hexes keep their fully green border (already
  shipped; unchanged).
- **Coordinates on tiles.** Every rendered tile shows its axial coordinates `(q,r)`
  on the tile at the readable tile font size, alongside the aggression badge and the
  ownership discriminator.
- **Spatial arrow navigation with the hangar reachable (producer Q3 = b).**
  Up/Down/Left/Right move focus spatially across the displayed hexes via the shared
  `FocusManager` grid mode, and the `◀ HANGAR` row is folded into that grid so
  arrows reach it too (Tab/Shift+Tab keep their linear cycling).
- **Parity, regression and validation.** `GymHexWar` renders the identical map
  (same pure model + shared renderer; a duplicated/copied body is rejected by
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`); ring-2 hexes remain playable — reveal is
  progressive, not removal of ring 2 content (proven by a test holding a ring-1 hex
  and asserting its ring-2 neighbours appear); ownership discrimination and grid
  navigation are covered by focused tests. All related documentation is updated to
  reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or
  docs entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A Hangar War player can now read the war at a glance — only the enemy hexes they
can actually reach are shown, every tile carries its coordinates and a
colourblind-safe ownership marker, owned hexes can be inspected without any risk of
re-deploying, and the arrow keys steer them spatially right to the hangar.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** The map's model (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`)
  and renderer (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`) are consumed by both `HexMapScene`
  and `GymHexWar`; every change lands in the shared modules — never a divergent copy.
- **Pure view.** Reveal/ownership/selection rules live in the pure model or the
  layout renderer, never in a scene; the scene stays a thin wiring layer
  (`HexMapScene.ts` handlers, `GymHexWar.ts` read-only).
- **Attract traversal consistency.** `decideMapAction`/`pickAttractHex` must never
  target a hex the map does not display; candidates stay anchored to
  hangar-or-held adjacency (Q1 = a).
- **Reuse, don't reinvent navigation.** Spatial arrows use the shipped
  `FocusManager` grid mode (`AH-0MV1BKZ0J00946EX`); no new input framework.
- **No backend; `localStorage` only** (GDD §6.6), unchanged. Warehouse rules:
  implementation is a later work item (tests via `/skill:test`, `CHANGELOG.md` only
  touched by the ship skill, UK English).

## Existing state (repository survey, dev `@` current)

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (shared renderer, ~470 lines): draws **all**
  `model.hexes` (every ring, held or not); a held hex's whole perimeter is already
  stroked green (`HELD_LINE`) — the "green borders" requirement is satisfied today;
  unheld tiles use `0xff6666`, label text is a single light-blue `TEXT_COLOR` for
  both; navigation is **linear** (Tab/arrow cycling via `FocusManager`, default
  mode); held hexes are not focusable ("nothing to deploy at").
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` (pure model): `HexIntel.actionable = !held`
  conflates "focusable" and "deployable"; `focusOrder` = every actionable hex +
  hangar row; `pickAttractHex` already implements hangar-or-held adjacency for the
  bot but **falls back** to "weakest unheld anywhere" when no adjacent hex exists —
  incompatible with a reveal-only map; `tileLabel = 'AGG n'` (no coordinates).
- `src/utils/focusManager.ts`: grid navigation (`navigation: 'grid', columns`) ships
  and is used by the gym menu (`AH-0MV1BKZ0J00946EX`) — left/right move between
  columns, up/down within a column, Tab linear.
- Tests pinning current behaviour and needing update: `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`
  (ring 2 renders with zero held hexes, held hex `focusRow` returns `false`, rows =
  all hex keys + hangar, `row.label === 'AGG n'`), `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts`
  (`actionable`/`tileLabel`/`focusOrder`), `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`
  (label + non-actionable rows).
- Attract traversal: `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` consumes `pickAttractHex` output
  on the map.

## Desired change

- **Model (`hexIntel.ts`):** per-hex `displayed` (adjacent to hangar ∪ held),
  separate `selectable` (focusable, every displayed hex) vs `actionable`/deployable
  (unheld only), `focusOrder` and grid columns over displayed hexes + hangar row,
  ring-progress lines computed over the full stored ring (progress is not lost when
  hexes are hidden), and `pickAttractHex` constrained to displayed/adjacent hexes
  with no off-map fallback.
- **Renderer (`hexMap.ts`):** draw only displayed hexes; tile label becomes
  `(q,r)` + `AGG n` + ownership discriminator; text colour blue (held) / orange
  (unheld) with the discriminator glyph; build grid columns (spatial left/right/
  up/down) with the `◀ HANGAR` row folded in as an extra row so arrows reach it;
  held hexes selectable (focus shows intel; activation no-ops).
- **Scene wiring:** `HexMapScene`/`GymHexWar` keep their thin handlers; rows gained
  selection semantics flow through the shared view.
- **Tests updated/added:** reveal (ring 2 appears only via held neighbours),
  selection vs deploy, CVD-safe discrimination, grid arrows reaching hexes and the
  hangar, attract-bot never hiding.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — reveal-filtered drawing, `(q,r)` + discriminator
  labels, CVD-safe text colours, grid columns incl. the hangar row, held-hex
  selection (focusable, non-deploying).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — `displayed`/`selectable`/`actionable` split,
  reveal rule (hangar ∪ held adjacency), grid-column order, full-ring progress lines,
  `pickAttractHex` restricted to displayed hexes.
- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` — grid-mode columns wiring (no functional change
  expected; columns supplied by the renderer).
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` — attract deploy constrained to displayed hexes.
- Tests: `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `README.md` (only if the map description changes).

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed): the map
  this item refines (shared renderer/model).
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** — Text on hex map is unreadable (completed): tile-label
  sizing and the detail-panel pattern this item builds on.
- **AH-0MV1BKZ0J00946EX** — Navigation of Gym menu (completed): shipped
  `FocusManager` grid mode reused here.
- **AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP** — Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal
  (completed): the map's traversal seam the reveal must stay consistent with.
- **AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE** — Build Candidate D epic (completed): parent design of

- **AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP** — Defense report should be rolled into the hex map screen
  (in-progress): **shared surface — do not build in isolation.** It rolls the
  attack report into the map (arrows + a left-hand attack-detail panel on selected
  hexes) and therefore builds on this item's owned-hex selection and spatial
  navigation. The two land the selection/panel mechanism once, not twice; sequence
  this item's selection foundation first unless the producer decides otherwise.
  record (GDD §8, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — reveal hides ring-2 playability.** A reveal-only map could be read as
  deleting ring-2 content. Mitigation: ring-2 hexes stay in the stored ring and
  appear as soon as a neighbouring hex is held; AC6 pins this with a test.
- **Risk — attract traversal picks a hidden hex.** `pickAttractHex` currently falls
  back to any unheld hex; the reveal must constrain it to displayed/adjacent hexes
  or the demo deploys at a hex that is not on screen. Mitigation: model-level
  guard + traversal test (AC1/AC6).
- **Risk — grid arrows confound players who learned Tab/linear cycling.**
  Mitigation: Tab/Shift+Tab keep their linear cycling and the bottom hint line is
  updated to describe both.
- **Risk — scope creep into post-MVP hex variety / fog-of-war.** Distinct map
  reveals, hex personalities and landmarks are recorded as linked work items, not
  grown into this item.
- **Assumption A3 — ring progress stays full-ring.** `RING n — x/y HEXES HELD`
  continues to count the whole stored ring (hidden hexes included), so progress is
  never lost when hexes are hidden by the reveal.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (intake 2026-11-13)

- **Q1 — Adjacency anchor.** *Does the hangar at `(0,0)` count as "owned" for the
  "only show hexes adjacent to an owned hex" rule?*
  - (a) Hangar anchors the reveal — ring 1 always renders; later rings appear as
    their neighbours are held.
  - (b) Only held hexes anchor — a brand-new map shows nothing until the first
    capture.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — a fresh war stays immediately legible and matches how
    `pickAttractHex` already defines neighbourhoods.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-11-13): (a)**. Source: interactive reply; recorded as AC
    "Adjacency-only reveal".
- **Q2 — Colourblind-safe encoding.** *Strict red-for-enemy / green-for-owned tile
  text is not safely distinguishable by colour-blind players; how should ownership
  colouring work?*
  - (a) Keep red/green text **and** add a non-colour per-tile discriminator.
  - (b) **Swap to a CVD-safe pair (blue/orange) plus a label discriminator.**
  - (c) Red/green text only, relying on the existing tile border/fill.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — preserves the producer's original direction while meeting
    the "colourblind friendly" requirement.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-11-13): (b)** — CVD-safe blue/orange text plus a
    non-colour label discriminator. Source: interactive reply; recorded as AC
    "CVD-safe ownership colouring".
- **Q3 — Spatial arrows vs the HANGAR row.** *With spatial up/down/left/right arrow
  navigation on the hex grid, how does the `◀ HANGAR` row stay reachable?*
  - (a) Arrows move spatially across displayed hexes only; HANGAR stays a bottom row
    reached via Tab/click.
  - (b) **Fold the HANGAR row into the arrow grid as an extra row/column so arrows
    reach it too.**
  - (c) Keep linear cycling.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — smallest change to the shipped linear-to-grid wiring.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-11-13): (b)**. Source: interactive reply; recorded as AC
    "Spatial arrow navigation with the hangar reachable".
- **Assumption A1 — "select owned hexes" (no question).** Selecting a held hex means
  focusing it so the detail panel shows its full intel; activating it never deploys
  (it is already the player's). Recorded as AC "Owned hexes selectable, never
  deployable".
- **Assumption A2 — green borders (no question).** The renderer already strokes a
  held hex's whole perimeter green; retained unchanged.

# Reduce length of hexmap battles (AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS)

## Impact

A Hangar War player's sortie is cut from ten waves to five — the level's
first four regular waves then the mini-boss on wave 5 — so taking a hex is a
snappier, bounded fight that still ends on the boss beat and grants the
reward.

## Problem statement

Hexmap (Hangar War) battles are too long: a deployment currently plays the
hex's aggression-selected campaign level through all **10 waves** (9 regular
+ the wave-10 mini-boss) before it resolves as a victory. The producer wants
the sortie shortened to **5 waves** so each hex is won in a tighter session.

## Users

- **As a Hangar War player**, I want a hex deployment to end after five waves
  — four regular waves then the hex's mini-boss on wave 5 — so the battle is
  short enough to dispatch one hex per sitting without losing the boss-beat
  payoff (producer answers Q1 = B, Q4: the mini-boss still resolves the
  capture and its reward still applies).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hex deployment (any ring, any aggression) plays **exactly 5 waves** of
  the hex's aggression-selected level: waves 1–4 are the level's regular
  waves and wave 5 is the level's mini-boss encounter. Defeating the wave-5
  mini-boss resolves the capture exactly as today (salvage banked, hex held,
  authored grant awarded, defender left, run ends as a victory) and is
  followed by the report → reward → map ordering, unchanged.
- The mini-boss spawned on wave 5 is the selected level's authored design
  (identity, patterns, player-power-scaled hit pool, and the deployed hex
  profile / grant demonstration when a hangar-war deployment is active),
  spawned through the existing `miniBossActive` seam; the arcade run
  (`▶ Play Game`) still plays all 10 waves of every level, byte-for-byte
  unchanged.
- Wave truncation is total and deterministic: a level with fewer than 5 waves
  flags its last wave as the mini-boss wave; the transform covers both the
  static `LEVELS` campaign and the sequenced (`buildSequencedLevels`)
  campaign; it never mutates the shared authored data.
- Tests cover the change: the truncation helper is unit-tested (5th wave
  becomes the mini-boss wave, sub-5 totals, both campaign sources, arcade
  untouched) and a deployment-level test asserts the run ends on the wave-5
  mini-boss defeat with the capture cycle resolving; no difficulty is
  changed by this item.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §8.2, the
  `hangarDeployment` module docs, `WaveManager` comments and any "wave-10
  mini-boss" references, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, and the ring-timing
  deployment model).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No difficulty change.** The producer explicitly removed the "increase the
  difficulty by 50%" requirement (Q2: "Ignore this part entirely"). This item
  changes battle **length only**; the aggression → level mapping, the
  difficulty-curve rows and all multipliers stay as shipped.
- **Universal scope.** The 5-wave rule applies to every hex deployment —
  every ring and every aggression (Q3).
- **Arcade untouched.** Only the hangar-war deployment path changes; the
  shipped 10-level arcade campaign and its wave-10 mini-bosses are
  preserved (gym↔game parity: the arcade behaviour is not in scope and no
  authored level data changes).
- **Mini-boss ending preserved.** The capture cycle, the report → reward →
  map win ordering, the salvage banking and the defender-required hold rule
  are all unchanged — only the wave the mini-boss sits on moves from 10
  to 5 (Q4).
- **Pure transform.** The truncation must be a pure, deterministic function
  over `LevelDefinition`s (no Phaser, no storage writes), consistent with the
  repo's module conventions; injected through the existing `setLevels` seam so
  the scene's spawn/progression machinery is untouched.

## Existing state (researched, with evidence)

- **Deployment model.** `buildHangarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`)
  launches a normal run at the hex's aggression-selected campaign level
  (`startLevel`); `PlayScene` calls `waveManager.beginGame(startLevel)` on the
  resolved campaign (`resolveCampaignLevels` in `PlayScene.ts`, which applies
  level enemy-count scaling to the static `LEVELS` or the sequenced
  `buildSequencedLevels` campaign). Each authored level has **10 waves**, with
  wave 10 flagged `miniBoss: true` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`).
- **Mini-boss ending (shipped).** `WaveManager` opens a per-level mini-boss
  encounter when a wave carries the `miniBoss` flag (`onEnemyDestroyed`,
  `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`); `PlayScene._spawnMiniBossIfDue()` spawns the
  level's `MiniBoss` (design `miniBossDesignForLevel`, hex profile via
  `hexMiniBossConfigForLevel`), and on its defeat `_resolveHangarWarCapture()`
  resolves the capture and the run ends as a victory (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2).
  The machinery keys on the `miniBoss` flag and the level design, **not** the
  wave number — so relocating the flag to wave 5 needs no encounter changes.
- **No existing 5-wave concept.** No authored or sequenced level truncates to
  5 waves today; the GDD §8.2 and module docs state "ends on that level's
  wave-10 mini-boss", so every such reference must be updated.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure helper that builds deployment levels from a resolved campaign:
   each level keeps its first 5 waves and wave 5 is flagged `miniBoss: true`
   (a level with fewer than 5 waves flags its last wave). Covers static
   `LEVELS` and sequenced campaigns because it operates on resolved
   `LevelDefinition[]`.
2. In `PlayScene.create()`, when a hangar-war deployment is active, inject the
   truncated campaign through `waveManager.setLevels(truncatedCampaign, { injected: true })`
   before `beginGame(startLevel)`. The arcade path is untouched (no
   deployment → resolved campaign as today).
3. Update "wave-10 mini-boss" prose to "wave-5 mini-boss" in the deployment
   model docs/comments (GDD §8.2, `hangarDeployment.ts`, `WaveManager.ts`
   deployment note, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D notes, and the
   ring-timing deployment model) without changing the arcade documentation.
4. Coordinate with the in-progress ring-timing re-measurement
   (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A), whose "one level ends on its wave-10 clear" model is
   superseded by the 5-wave deployment — record the interaction on that item
   (its measurements must model a 5-wave sortie; the arena plays the level's
   authored waves, so the harness learns the truncated wave count from the
   same helper, kept out of scope here).

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — deployment launch contract; module docs state the "wave-10 mini-boss" ending; a placement candidate for the pure 5-wave transform (or a new sibling module under `src/core/hangarWar/`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `create()` injects the truncated campaign via `waveManager.setLevels({ injected: true })` when `hangarWarDeployment` is set; `miniBossConfigFor`/`_spawnMiniBossIfDue`/`_resolveHangarWarCapture` are unchanged consumers.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `beginGame`/`setLevels` seams + deployment comment that names "wave-10 mini-boss".
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — authored `LEVELS` (10 waves, wave-10 `miniBoss` flag) — read-only input; do not mutate.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — sequenced campaign source the transform must also cover.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — new tests for the truncation + 5-wave deployment end.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — deployment-model prose to update.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.*` — deployment-model references for the ring-timing coordination note.

## Related work

- **In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the hex (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2)** — completed; shipped the mini-boss ending this item re-points from wave 10 to wave 5. Its docs child (AH-0MWCOW7KO004D3EF) pinned the "wave-10" phrasing this item updates.
- **Re-measure ring timing for one-level hex deployments (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A)** — in-progress (plan_complete); models a deployment as the level's full wave set ending on its wave-10 clear. This item changes the shipped sortie to 5 waves, so the harness's deployment model must follow; record the interaction (output of this item's plan step; do not absorb its scope).
- **HexMap aggression increases too quickly (AH-0MWB9V9Q3004HD2P)** — completed epic; the strength-budgeted frontier the difficulty model rests on (unchanged here — no difficulty change).
- **Tests: one-level deployment semantics (AH-0MWCQ4EZD006YWHV)** — open; blocked on the ring-timing item; pins one-level deployment semantics in the harness that the 5-wave change will also affect (coordinate, do not edit).
- **Gym parity:** `GymMiniBoss` (HEX mode) exercises the hex-profile deployment mini-boss and is unaffected — the encounter config is unchanged; no combat gym plays a deployment's wave count, so no gym row changes (verified against `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).

### Related work (automated report)

- **Design and implement the pure difficulty scorer module (AH-0MUDIV437000U4NY)** — completed; the enemy-difficulty scorer is related to the *dropped* 50 % difficulty requirement — out of scope here, no difficulty change.
- **Tests: one-level deployment semantics (AH-0MWCQ4EZD006YWHV)** — open; pins one-level deployment semantics in the ring-timing harness that the 5-wave change will also affect (coordinate, do not edit).
- **Replace fixed-duration dive with fixed-speed dive (AH-0MW3MWRZ5003KVR3)** — completed; unrelated dive-tuning precedent, no interaction with wave count.
- **Repo file matches:** `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, `docs/BALANCING.md` — the GDD is updated by this item; `README`/`BALANCING` only if they name the wave-10 deployment ending (checked during docs work).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: scope bleed into the arcade campaign.** The truncation gate must be
  *only* the hangar-war deployment branch; any leak would shorten the arcade
  and break its "10 waves" contracts. Mitigation: inject through
  `setLevels({ injected: true })` in the deployment branch only, and pin the
  arcade path with an existing-suite regression test.
- **Risk: sequenced campaign reshape.** The sequenced campaign rebuilds
  waves at run start and its curve length sets each level's wave count; the
  transform must run on resolved levels before `beginGame` regardless of
  source. Mitigation: unit-test both `LEVELS` and a sequenced sample.
- **Risk: mini-boss spawn gating on the 5th wave.** Wave 5 already has
  authored group content; flagging it may interact with the level-identity /
  no-adjacent-same-composition invariants. The flag is applied at runtime
  (never to authored data) and the composition contracts in
  `campaignVariety.test.ts` read the static data, so they stay green —
  verify in the change.
- **Assumption: waves 1–4 keep their authored content** and only the flag
  moves to wave 5 (the level's authored wave-10 composition is dropped with
  waves 6–10); confirmed by Q1 = B (mini-boss at wave 5), with the reward
  still applying (Q4).
- **Assumption: sub-5 levels flag their last wave** (a conservative total
  fallback; static levels all have 10 waves, so this is defensive only).
- **Scope-creep guard:** updating the ring-timing harness to the 5-wave
  deployment, re-balancing ring budgets, and any difficulty change are
  explicitly out of scope and tracked elsewhere
  (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A and its children).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does '5 waves' mean in context? (A) end after 5 regular waves with no mini-boss; (B) end at wave 5 with the mini-boss at that point; (C) something else?" — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (B)** — mini-boss at wave 5. Source: reply to intake questions on AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS (comment AH-C0MWESTZG1006FUPM).
- Q: "What does 'increase the difficulty by 50%' mean? (A) aggression +50 %; (B) all difficulty-curve values +50 % for deployments; (C) mini-boss HP +50 %; (D) other?" — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "Ignore this part entirely"** — the difficulty increase is dropped from scope; this item is length-only. Source: reply to intake questions on AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS.
- Q: "Does this apply universally or conditionally (ring / aggression dependent)?" — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): universally** — every hex deployment, every ring and aggression. Source: reply to intake questions on AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS.
- Q: "With the end at wave 5: does a mini-boss still trigger, and does its reward still apply?" — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** mini-boss at wave 5, reward still applies — the capture cycle and the report → reward → map ordering are unchanged. Source: reply to intake questions on AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS.
- **Research note:** the mini-boss machinery (WaveManager `miniBoss` flag → `_spawnMiniBossIfDue` → `_resolveHangarWarCapture`) is wave-number-agnostic, so no encounter code needs to change; only the flag's position and the docs move. Inspected `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`miniBossActive` seam, capture on mini-boss defeat), `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`, `src/waves/Formations.ts` (wave-10 flags), GDD §8.2 and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (no combat gym plays a deployment's wave count).

# Goal

As a player, I want hulls to be able to grant **extra upgrade bays** (more equipment/loadout slots than the base hull) as a special-reward axis, so the special-mission reward space is not limited to more hit points.

Follow-on from the producer's answer to Q2 on **AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55** ("2. A — create a work item to add upgrade bays"): the special-missions item ships its first reward as a hull with extra hit points; the **upgrade-bay concept does not yet exist in the data model** (HullRunStats carries only startingLives + speedMultiplier; upgrades are armour/firepower/systems), so extending the run-stats/loadout model for upgrade bays is tracked separately here.

Part of the Hangar War's **post-MVP mitigation backlog** (discovered-from:AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55, recorded in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and GDD §8.2).

## Scope

- Introduce an **upgrade-bay concept** to the hangar hull model: a hull authoring how many bays (equipment/loadout slots) it deploys with, resolved into the run loadout and persisted under the existing `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload.
- Futures a hull reward that grants **extra upgrade bays** rather than (or in addition to) extra hit points — the second special reward the design of record names.
- Must reuse the shipped deployment path (`PlayScene` + `src/scenes/core/`) and the pure hangar economy; no second run implementation (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity). Gym coverage `GymHangar`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hull definition can author an upgrade-bay count, and the resolved deployment/loadout honours it (shipped run, no divergent copy).
- The bay count is persisted under the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload with field-presence migration (no new storage key).
- `GymHangar` exercises the bay/bay-resolution behaviour with the same code as the game.
- Tests pin the bay model, the loadout resolution and the persistence round-trip; full suite green.

# Driven worktrees fork from a diverged local `dev`, so children start on a stale base

## Problem

`implement.py start` refreshes the local parent branch before `git worktree add`,
but `_sync_parent_branch` **skips** the refresh when the local `dev` ref is
diverged or cannot be fetched non-checked-out (`reason:
"diverged_or_checked_out"`). The worktree is then forked from that stale local
`dev` anyway, and the child session inherits a base that is missing commits
already published on `origin/dev`.

Observed during AH-0MWF0CS4I001XZHU (driven child of AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55):

- the main checkout's `dev` was `ahead 1, behind 8` of `origin/dev`
  (`e38797b8` local-only, duplicating `9687a6db`'s content);
- the worktree forked at `e38797b8`, so its changed-scope test gate ran an
  unrelated `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` against the pre-fix source and went
  **red** on a failure `origin/dev` had already fixed (`HANGAR_WAR_SCENE_KEYS`
  still listing the deleted `DefenceReportScene`);
- the session had to rebase onto `origin/dev` (8d1c1aca) by hand before it could
  pass its gate and push.

The same symptom is recorded in AH-0MWEYVRUX008SLJ8's completion comments ("Push
to dev initially failed (non-fast-forward …). Rebased onto origin/dev and
retried"), so this is recurring, not a one-off.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree forked by `start` is based on a ref that is a fast-forward ancestor of
`origin/<parent>`, so a driven child never starts behind the published base.

Suggested approach (needs a decision): when the local parent branch is diverged
or cannot be updated, fork the worktree from `origin/<parent>` instead of the
stale local ref (the local ref can stay untouched), and record that choice in the
start comment. Alternatively, report the divergence loudly as a WARNING with the
ahead/behind counts so the session knows why its gate may be red.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `implement.py start` never forks a worktree from a local parent
  branch that is behind `origin/<parent>`: either the local ref is fast-forwarded
  or the worktree is forked from `origin/<parent>`.
- **AC2** — The start report/comment names the base ref used and, when the local
  parent branch was skipped (diverged / checked out / lock held), states why and
  the ahead/behind counts.
- **AC3** — A driven child started from a diverged local `dev` passes its first
  changed-scope gate without a manual rebase (regression test with a synthetic
  diverged local branch).
- **AC4** — Existing behaviour is preserved: a lock-held or fetch-failed refresh
  still fails open (never blocks `start`) and never force-updates a diverged
  branch.

## Related work

- discovered-from: AH-0MWF0CS4I001XZHU (the driven child that hit it)
- AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB (completed): "implement.py finish leaves local dev behind
  after pushing to remote dev" — related stale-local-dev symptom
- AH-0MWEYVRUX008SLJ8 comments: hand-rebased after a non-fast-forward push

## Impact

Driven child sessions start from the published base, so they stop burning a
rebase and a red gate on work someone else already shipped.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB** – implement.py finish leaves local dev behind after pushing to remote dev (completed)
- **AH-0MVBMRK6X0069QDI** – Game-side uploader fired at run end (completed)
- **AH-0MUZJDT88002L536** – Worktree builds fail: build-audio cannot resolve the sibling ToneForge CLI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+128 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+125 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+118 more)


## Plan

This item is the **AI Hell discovery report** for an agent-infrastructure defect:
`implement.py` lives in the SorraAgents skills repo
(`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, reached
via `~/.pi/agent/skills`), not in this repo. Following the producer precedent recorded
on AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB (2026-09-25: "implementation is in the SorraAgents project …
no implementation change is required in AI_Hell"), the actionable fix and its
regression tests are tracked in the SorraAgents counterpart, and this item stays a
discovery report with **no AI Hell children**.

**Counterpart:** SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK — "implement.py start forks a driven worktree from
a diverged local dev" (tag `discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2`), which carries AC1–AC4
verbatim and is decomposed test-first into:

| Work item | Scope | Order |
|---|---|---|
| SA-0MWFFXKKA005CLVK | Test-first: `start` base-ref harness (diverged fixture) + characterisation of the current fail-open behaviour — lands green | 1 |
| SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX | Fork the worktree from `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` when the local parent is behind; record base ref + reason + ahead/behind in the report and the start comment — red-first cases written in this worktree, tests and fix land together | 2 (depends on 1) |
| SA-0MWFFXQNT002LB8T | Document the base-ref rule and the new report keys in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and `skill/implement/SKILL.md` | 3 (depends on 2) |

**Decision on the report's "needs a decision" fork:** the two suggested approaches are
complementary, not alternatives. AC1 requires never forking from a local parent branch
that is behind `origin/<parent>`, so the fix forks from `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`
whenever the local parent is behind (which includes the diverged case) and leaves the
local ref untouched; AC2 then requires the report/comment to name the base ref and, when
the refresh was skipped (diverged / checked out / lock held), the reason plus the
ahead/behind counts. A local-ahead-only `dev` (`behind == 0`) keeps the local base, so
unpublished local commits are never dropped; a fetch failure keeps the current local-base

`skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py` (new),
`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.

No AI Hell code, gym or gameplay surface is touched, so the gym↔game parity convention
does not apply.

  loudly) should be implemented?**
  Answer (agent, resolved from this item's ACs + code reading): both. AC1 forbids
  forking from a local parent that is behind `origin/<parent>` (fork from the published
  ref when the local ref cannot be fast-forwarded), and AC2 mandates reporting the reason
  and ahead/behind counts. Evidence: this item's AC1/AC2; `_sync_parent_branch`

  Final: fork from `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` when `behind > 0`.

  Answer (agent, from documented producer precedent): no. `implement.py` is agent
  infrastructure that lives in the SorraAgents repo; the precedent on

**OPEN QUESTIONS:** none — no answer was required from the producer to plan this item.

# Concurrent session edits the main checkout, tripping the finish gate's live-repo mutation guard

## Problem statement

During a parallel docs session (AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ), writes landed in the main checkout instead of the session's own linked worktree. When `implement.py finish` ran on another child (AH-0MWEWYZLQ0078G0D), the changed-scope test gate detected the live-repo mutation and aborted — blocking otherwise-complete work.

## Users

- Agent sessions that run in linked worktrees and need `implement.py finish` to pass their changed-scope test gate.
- Operator reviewing CI-quality gates who expects the gate to reflect the item's own changes only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Identify the session that wrote into the main checkout and ensure its changes are confined to (or discarded from) its own worktree — no concurrent session should mutate the main checkout.
2. The main checkout is left clean after concurrent sessions end; any untracked files (e.g. `src/test/playSceneBootGuard.test.ts`) are accounted for and not left to block finish gates.
3. Re-running `implement.py finish AH-0MWEWYZLQ0078G0D` (and any other blocked child) passes the changed-scope gate with no live-repo mutation false positive.
4. Where the harness can, the worktree-isolation gate fails closed when a session's writes resolve into the main checkout or a sibling worktree — the parent phase already reports this class of issue; harden the detection to trigger *before* the finish gate (e.g. in `phase_start` or early in `implement.py finish`) so the offending session can be stopped proactively.

## Impact

A concurrent session writing into the main checkout can block otherwise-complete work from landing, and a corrupted or ambiguous checkout could be incorrectly attributed to an unrelated item if the guard were absent.

## Constraints

- Changes must not alter the existing `implement.py finish` contract — only strengthen its preconditions.
- The worktree-isolation gate must not break legitimate scenarios (e.g. the operator's own intended changes in the main checkout).

## Existing state

- The live-repo mutation guard in `implement.py finish` detects tracked-file changes mid-run and aborts.
- The parent phase reports when a session's writes land outside its worktree, but this is a diagnostic, not a pre-check.
- The concurrent session (AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ) has since completed and moved its work into its own worktree.
- The main checkout is now clean (only an untracked test file remains).

## Desired change

1. Harden the worktree-isolation check so it runs early (before the changed-scope test gate) and fails closed on a session writing outside its worktree.
2. Add documentation to AGENTS.md about the worktree-isolation invariant and the consequences of violating it.
3. Ensure blocked items can be unblocked once the main checkout is clean.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** Hardening the gate must not change the existing `implement.py finish` contract; only strengthen its preconditions.
- **False positives:** The gate must not flag the operator's own intended changes in the main checkout.
- **Assumption:** The parent phase's existing diagnostic can be promoted to a pre-check without architectural changes.
- **Assumption:** The fix does not need to address the root cause of *why* AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ wrote to the main checkout — only detect and prevent it earlier.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `finish` phase and live-repo mutation guard
- `skill/shared/` — worktree isolation helpers
- `AGENTS.md` (project) — worktree-isolation documentation

## Related work

- AH-0MWEWYZLQ0078G0D — blocked by the live-repo mutation (still unpushed commits in its worktree)
- AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ — the concurrent session that wrote into the main checkout (now completed)

- AH-0MVSRO0MM004T450 — mid-run checkout must not mint spurious test-failure items (completed)
- AH-0MUIIJ3820034WAZ — test-skill live-repo mutation guard false-positives (completed)

No clarifying questions were asked — the work item description was sufficiently detailed to proceed with the intake brief.

   reintroduce the flake.

a pausing reward overlay on an **already-finished** run; the player then faces a
run-scoped upgrade choice whose effect is void, and the screen change waits on
it. This is the same "run-scoped reward applied to a completed run" principle
the producer already ruled against for the hangar win path
(AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2, Q1 = (c)). The hold-full choice lives only in

have no `runFinished`), so the guard is a game-only no-op in the gyms — to be
confirmed and recorded against `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

1. **Test + diagnostics for the victory-path stall** (`task`, high) — reproduce

2. **Harden deterministic stepping** (`task`, high) — one shared hold-full

   Depends on 1.
3. **Suppress the hold-full choice after the run finishes** (`bug`, medium) —
   stop offering a void reward on a won run. Depends on 1.
4. **Docs + full-suite verification** (`docs`, medium) — README testing
   conventions, flake lineage, and the shipped green suite. Depends on 2 and 3.

### Phasing decision

This is **not** a phased epic: the four children are sequential increments of a
single defect (reproduce → harness hardening → product guard → document and
verify), each carrying its own tests and doc touch. No horizontal layer is
deferred, so no between-phase review gate is required; items 2 and 3 each update
the next item's description if the reproduction in item 1 changes the diagnosis.

### Documented assumptions

1. The stall is the hold-full pause inside the boss-kill / victory-hold window
   (evidence above); a widening of `stepUntil`'s budget is **not** the fix,
   because a paused scene ignores time entirely.
2. The fix stays inside test harness helpers plus one narrow `PlayScene` guard —
   no boss, wave, reward or balance changes.
3. The stray untracked `src/test/playSceneBootGuard.test.ts` in the main
   checkout is already tracked elsewhere (AH-0MWFI3BLE000JMRU,
   AH-0MWFHXYGW003L1VM) and must not be edited or deleted by this work.

  repository evidence (source, worklog history, prior items) and recorded in the
  RCA above; no question was put to the producer in this session.

- **OPEN QUESTION (producer; non-blocking, resolved by feature 1):** is the
  hold-full-during-victory pause reachable by a human player (a live product
  defect: a void reward overlay on a won run, whose selection gates the
  GameOverScene transition), or only reachable through deterministic test
  stepping? Feature 1's reproduction records the answer; if it is
  human-reachable, feature 3 is a product fix (with gym-parity note) rather than
  a test-only guard. Planning proceeds on the conservative assumption that it is
  reachable and worth guarding.

## Problem statement

dev's `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` carried committed Git merge-conflict markers
(`<<<<<<< HEAD` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> ef87a124`) from an earlier merge, so the
published parity matrix contained two nested three-way conflict blocks that

sides' content (commit `fd68cd53`, child `AH-0MWEWYZLQ0078G0D`), but nothing
detects a recurrence: the existing docs guard
(`src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`) validates scene coverage, verdicts

dev again unnoticed.

## Users

- **The maintainer / parity-sweep owner** reading the matrix to decide whether a
  gym has diverged.

    row's verdict without decoding conflict noise.*
- **The agent making a gym↔game parity change**, sent to this file by `AGENTS.md`
  § Game Architecture Conventions.
  - *As an agent, I want a corrupted merge to fail the test suite, so I never
    read, act on or extend a half-merged matrix.*
- **The producer reviewing dev.**

    than by a human reader.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` contains no Git merge-conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`,

  the offending line numbers so the bad merge is actionable.

  into an in-memory copy (or a temporary fixture) of the real document and
  asserts the detector reports them — without mutating the repository, matching
  the existing red-before pattern in that file.
- The `Automated guard` panel in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` states that the guard
  also fails if the file contains merge-conflict markers, so the documented

A maintainer or agent reading `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` sees one clean parity matrix
instead of three-way conflict noise, and a future bad merge now fails the test
suite instead of quietly landing conflict markers on dev.

## Constraints

- **Preserve both sides.** The original merge's content on both sides is
  intentional: do not "resolve" the history by dropping the defending-bot-skills

- **Avoid false positives.** A bare `=======` line is also a legal Markdown

The dev-push full-suite gate is **red on `dev`**, which blocks every item's push.
Four scene tests in two suites still encode the **pre-win-path** world: three
assert bank balances from before the fixed win bonus was banked, and one asserts
that a winning deployment presents the mini-boss reward wheel over the paused
map — behaviour the shipped win path deliberately removed.

- **As a Hangar War player**, I want the win-path reward change to ship, so a
  won deployment pays into my persistent war instead of spinning a wheel whose
  upgrades vanish into a finished run.

  one-line change instead of a hunt through scene suites.

three of the four failures, and **incomplete** for the fourth:

| Suite / test | Actual cause |
